unit.label: Getting around & explicit comparison
unit.title: Which Way Is Faster?
unit.description: 10 new this lesson words and forms. Get around with Taiwan transport vocabulary and compare two choices explicitly with 比.

goal.pinyin: Qí jīchē bǐ zuò gōngchē kuài ma?
goal.meaning: Is riding a scooter faster than taking the bus?

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 8, Vocabulary II and Grammar V, pp. 163–171. This unit teaches a coherent transport/visit subset plus explicit 比; 古代 and 不行 remain for the following source-continuation unit.

lessons.title: Classmates and City Transport
lessons.subtitle: Learn classmate, MRT, and the everyday Taiwan word 公車.

steps.prompt: Which word is the usual Taiwan Mandarin short form for “bus”?
steps.explanation: 公車 is the common short form of 公共汽車 in Taiwan.

steps.prompt: Which word means “classmate”?
steps.explanation: 同學 means classmate; 學 is already familiar from 學生 and 學校.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 同 is tóng: same; together.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 捷 is jié: quick; first character of 捷運.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 公 is gōng: public.

lessons.title: Ride or Take a Taxi
lessons.subtitle: Talk about scooters, giving someone a ride, and taxis.

steps.prompt: Your classmate takes you somewhere on a scooter. Which verb describes giving you the ride?
steps.explanation: 載 means to carry someone or give someone a ride in or on a vehicle.

steps.prompt: Which word is Taiwan Mandarin for “taxi”?
steps.explanation: 計程車 is the standard Taiwan Mandarin word for taxi.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 騎 is qí: ride.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 計 is jì: calculate; first character of 計程車.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 程 is chéng: route; journey; measure.

steps.prompt: Which component occupies the left side of 騎?
steps.explanation: 馬 is the ten-stroke left component; 奇 is on the right.

steps.prompt: Which component is on the left of 計?
steps.explanation: 言 is the seven-stroke left component; 十 is the two-stroke right component.

lessons.title: Visit a School
lessons.subtitle: Use 參觀 for a visit to an institution and 差不多 for a small difference.

steps.prompt: Two travel times are roughly the same. Which expression fits?
steps.explanation: 差不多 means “about the same” here: the difference is small.

steps.prompt: Which verb means visiting and looking around an institution, such as a school?
steps.explanation: 參觀 is used for visiting an institution or site.

steps.prompt: Which group forms the bottom of 參?
steps.explanation: The last three descending slants form 彡.

lessons.title: Compare Two Things
lessons.subtitle: Name both sides explicitly with 比.

steps.prompt: Which sentence explicitly says taking the MRT is faster than taking the train?
steps.explanation: A 比 B + property explicitly names both items being compared.

steps.prompt: In A 比 B 快, which item is described as faster?
steps.explanation: The property after B describes A relative to B.

steps.prompt: Our school is farther away than their school. Which keeps the comparison direction?
options: 我們學校比他們學校遠。
他們學校比我們學校遠。
steps.answer: 我們學校比他們學校遠。
steps.explanation: The farther school is A, before 比. Reversing A and B reverses the claim.

lessons.title: Not Faster Than
lessons.subtitle: Negate the comparison and avoid a common degree-adverb error.

steps.prompt: Which sentence means “Taking the bus is not faster than taking a taxi”?
options: 坐公車不比坐計程車快。
坐公車比不坐計程車快。
steps.answer: 坐公車不比坐計程車快。
steps.explanation: 不 goes before 比 to negate the comparison.

steps.prompt: Which basic 比 sentence is correct?
steps.explanation: In the basic 比 pattern, degree adverbs such as 很 and 非常 do not appear before the property.

steps.prompt: A 不比 B 快 says A is not faster than B. Could they be equally fast?
steps.explanation: Not faster excludes greater speed; it does not exclude equal speed.

steps.prompt: Which says this phone is not more expensive than that one?
steps.explanation: 不 precedes 比. The basic comparison also does not take 很 before 貴.

lessons.title: Choose a Ride
lessons.subtitle: Contrast implicit 比較 with explicit 比 and recycle 又…又….

steps.prompt: The comparison target is already understood. Which says “The MRT is relatively faster”?
steps.explanation: 比較 can leave the comparison target implicit; 比 needs an explicit B.

steps.prompt: Which sentence gives two qualities of High Speed Rail?
steps.explanation: 又…又… joins two qualities of the same subject.

steps.prompt: Both routes take the same time. Which answer fits “騎機車比坐公車快嗎？”?
steps.explanation: 差不多 reports little difference; the other answers claim one choice is faster.

steps.prompt: Which explicitly names both items in a price comparison?
steps.explanation: 比 names the second item 那支; 比較 leaves it understood; 又…又… links properties.

lessons.title: Unit 25 Review
lessons.subtitle: Transport vocabulary, visiting, and explicit comparison.

steps.prompt: Which sentence explicitly compares two transportation choices?
steps.explanation: 比 explicitly names A and B.

steps.prompt: Which expression means “about the same”?
steps.explanation: 差不多 means about the same.

steps.prompt: Which sentence correctly negates an explicit comparison?
options: 坐公車不比坐計程車快。
坐公車比坐計程車不快。
steps.answer: 坐公車不比坐計程車快。
steps.explanation: In this pattern, 不 precedes 比.

steps.prompt: Which sentence says THIS phone costs more, not the other one?
steps.explanation: 這支手機 is A, the item described as more expensive.

steps.prompt: If 坐公車不比坐計程車快 is true, which possibility remains?
steps.explanation: 不比…快 rules out “faster” but allows equal speed.

steps.prompt: Choose the basic 比 sentence without an unsuitable degree adverb.
steps.explanation: Do not insert 很 before the final property in this basic comparison.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 同 is tóng: same; together.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 捷 is jié: quick; first character of 捷運.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 騎 is qí: ride.

steps.prompt: Listen and choose the character you hear.
steps.explanation: 計 is jì: calculate; first character of 計程車.

steps.prompt: Which sentence says a classmate gives you a ride on a scooter?
steps.explanation: 騎機車 describes riding the scooter; 載我 says the classmate gives you the ride.

newVocabulary.note: In Taiwan, 機車 commonly refers to a motor scooter or motorcycle.

newVocabulary.meaning: to carry; give someone a ride in/on a vehicle

newVocabulary.note: Standard Taiwan Mandarin for a Mass Rapid Transit system.
Common Taiwan short form of 公共汽車.

同.note: 同 means same or together; 同學 is someone who studies alongside you, a classmate.
同.memory: The outer frame surrounds 一 and 口; keep the box balanced around the center.

parts.label: 冂
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The first two strokes make the tall outer frame, open at the bottom.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: inner horizontal
parts.description: The third stroke is the short horizontal inside the frame.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: inner mouth
parts.description: The last three strokes make a compact 口 below the inner bar.

同.partOrderLabel: outer frame, inner horizontal, then inner mouth
同.layoutLabel: outer frame around an inner bar and mouth

參.note: Use the first-tone reading cān in 參觀. Learn this word-specific reading rather than guessing from other words containing 參.
參.memory: Three 厶-like marks sit above the 人/彡 lower structure; keep the lower strokes open and descending.

parts.label: 厽
parts.name: three upper loops
parts.description: The first six strokes form three 厶-like loops in a triangle. Each loop uses two strokes.

parts.label: 人
parts.name: spreading middle
parts.description: The next two strokes spread outward below the three loops.

parts.label: 彡
parts.name: three lower slants
parts.description: The final three strokes descend diagonally underneath the spreading middle.

觀.note: 觀 is first-tone guān in 參觀. The 見 component on the right provides a useful visual connection to seeing.
觀.memory: The dense left side balances 見 on the right; leave enough width for the final 見 component.

parts.label: 雚
parts.name: dense left component
parts.description: The first eighteen paths form the dense left component in this licensed Taiwan glyph: the top cluster, two small boxes, and the lower bird-shaped block.

parts.label: 見
parts.name: seeing component
parts.description: The last seven strokes make 見: a tall 目 shape above two spreading lower strokes.

騎.note: 騎 means to ride astride, as on a scooter or bicycle. Here learn 騎機車; 坐 names taking transport such as a bus.
騎.memory: 馬 fills the left side and 奇 fills the right; keep both halves narrow enough to fit together.

parts.label: 馬
parts.name: horse component
parts.description: The first ten strokes form 馬 on the left, including its four lower dots.

parts.label: 奇
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last eight strokes form 奇, with 大 above the lower 可-shaped structure.

載.note: 載 is fourth-tone zài when it means carrying someone in a vehicle or giving them a ride. 載我 means give me a ride.
載.memory: The 車 element sits inside the larger 戈-like structure; keep the central 車 readable before the sweeping final strokes.

parts.label: outer
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The upper cross and long horizontal are written first; the curved 戈 strokes finish after the inner 車. These six highlighted strokes form one visual frame, but are not consecutive in writing order.

parts.label: 車
parts.name: inner vehicle component
parts.description: The seven middle strokes form 車 inside the surrounding frame. Follow the animation for the interleaved whole-character stroke order.

載.partOrderLabel: outer frame, then inner 車 (visual groups; writing strokes interleave)

捷.meaning: quick; first character of 捷運
捷.note: 捷 is second-tone jié. Learn it with 運 in 捷運, the Taiwan term for the MRT.
捷.memory: 扌 is the narrow left component; the right side carries most of the character’s width.

parts.label: 扌
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: The first three strokes make the narrow 扌 on the left.

parts.label: 疌
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last eight strokes form the wider right block, with a central vertical and spreading lower strokes.

公.note: 公 is first-tone gōng. In 公車, it forms the common Taiwan word for a bus.
公.memory: The two upper strokes spread like 八 above 厶; center the lower turn beneath them.

parts.label: 八
parts.name: upper spreading strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes open to the left and right above the lower loop.

parts.label: 厶
parts.name: lower loop
parts.description: The final bent stroke and dot make 厶 beneath the spreading top.

計.meaning: calculate; first character of 計程車
計.note: 計 is fourth-tone jì. 計程車 is the Taiwan word for taxi; keep the three syllables jì-chéng-chē distinct.
計.memory: 言 forms the left side and 十 the right; keep the left speech component compact and even.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form the narrow 言 on the left, ending in its small 口.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: right cross
parts.description: The last two strokes form 十 on the right: horizontal, then vertical.

程.note: 程 is second-tone chéng in 計程車. Its left component is 禾, not the speech component 言 in 計.
程.memory: 禾 is on the left and 呈 on the right; align the lower strokes so the character does not lean.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 禾 on the left, ending with its two lower side strokes.

parts.label: 呈
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last seven strokes form 呈, with 口 above the lower horizontal framework.

差.note: 差 is fourth-tone chà in 差不多. This expression says the difference is small, so the two things are about the same.
差.memory: The upper 羊-like strokes lead into 工 below; keep the lower 工 centered under the slanting middle stroke.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper sloping group
parts.description: The first six paths form the upper group: two short strokes, three horizontal levels, and the long left-falling stroke.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: lower work component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 工 beneath the upper group.

u25-bi-comparison.title: Explicit comparison with 比
u25-bi-comparison.pattern: A + 比 + B + state verb / property
u25-bi-comparison.explanation: Use 比 when you name both things being compared. A is described relative to B. Keep A and B comparable: compare two places, two objects, or two ways of travelling. Swapping A and B reverses the direction of the comparison.

examples.pinyin: Zuò jiéyùn bǐ zuò huǒchē kuài.
examples.meaning: Taking the MRT is faster than taking the train.

examples.text: 我們學校比他們學校遠。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào bǐ tāmen xuéxiào yuǎn.
examples.meaning: Our school is farther away than their school.

u25-bi-comparison.remember: 比較 can leave the comparison target understood; 比 explicitly names A and B.

u25-bi-negation.title: Negating a 比 comparison
u25-bi-negation.pattern: A + 不比 / 不是比 + B + property
u25-bi-negation.explanation: Either 不比 or 不是比 can negate an explicit comparison here. 不比 says A is not more X than B; 不是比 explicitly rejects the proposed comparison. “Not faster” does not necessarily mean “slower”: the speeds could be equal. 不比 rejects the claim that A exceeds B on this property.

examples.text: 坐公車不比坐計程車快。
examples.pinyin: Zuò gōngchē bù bǐ zuò jìchéngchē kuài.
examples.meaning: Taking the bus is not faster than taking a taxi.

examples.text: 坐公車不是比坐計程車快。
examples.pinyin: Zuò gōngchē bú shì bǐ zuò jìchéngchē kuài.
examples.meaning: It is not the case that taking the bus is faster than taking a taxi.

u25-bi-negation.remember: Put the negative before 比, not after the comparison target.

u25-bi-degree.title: No 很 inside the basic 比 frame
u25-bi-degree.explanation: In the basic 比 pattern taught here, degree adverbs such as 很, 真, and 非常 do not appear before the final state verb/property.

examples.pinyin: Zuò jiéyùn bǐ zuò huǒchē kuài.
examples.meaning: Taking the MRT is faster than taking the train.

u25-bi-degree.remember: Say A 比 B 快, not A 比 B 很快.

u25-mrt-school.meaning: I take the MRT to school.

u25-classmate-bus.meaning: I take the bus with my classmate.
u25-classmate-bus.note: 跟 introduces the companion before the main verb phrase.

u25-classmate-ride.meaning: My classmate gives me a ride on a scooter.
u25-classmate-ride.note: 騎 names riding the scooter; 載 names carrying/giving someone a ride.

u25-taxi.meaning: I want to take a taxi there.
u25-taxi.note: 計程車 is Taiwan Mandarin for taxi.

u25-visit-palace.pinyin: Wǒ gēn tóngxué qù cānguān xuéxiào.
u25-visit-palace.meaning: I am going with my classmate to look around a school.
u25-visit-palace.note: 參觀 means to visit and look around an institution or site, rather than simply going there for class.

u25-about-same.text: 騎機車跟坐公車差不多。

u25-about-same.meaning: Riding a scooter and taking the bus are about the same.
u25-about-same.note: 差不多 says the difference is small.

u25-mrt-faster.pinyin: Zuò jiéyùn bǐ zuò huǒchē kuài.
u25-mrt-faster.meaning: Taking the MRT is faster than taking the train.
u25-mrt-faster.note: A 比 B + property explicitly compares A with B.

u25-bus-not-faster.text: 坐公車不比坐計程車快。
u25-bus-not-faster.pinyin: Zuò gōngchē bù bǐ zuò jìchéngchē kuài.
u25-bus-not-faster.meaning: Taking the bus is not faster than taking a taxi.

u25-scooter-question.pinyin: Qí jīchē bǐ zuò gōngchē kuài ma?
u25-scooter-question.meaning: Is riding a scooter faster than taking the bus?
u25-scooter-question.note: This reinforces the comparison pattern in context.

u25-same-time.text: 騎機車跟坐公車差不多。
u25-same-time.pinyin: Qí jīchē gēn zuò gōngchē chàbuduō.
u25-same-time.meaning: Riding a scooter and taking the bus are about the same.
u25-same-time.note: A natural answer when the two travel times are close.

u25-phone-price.pinyin: Zhè zhī shǒujī bǐ nà zhī guì.
u25-phone-price.meaning: This phone is more expensive than that one.
u25-phone-price.note: The property 貴 describes the first phone relative to the second.
